statement: In Gemma 4 E2B (35 layers, 20 KV-shared), final-position outputs depend on earlier positions only through K/V computed in layers 0-14 (stored by layers 13/14); residual states of non-final positions entering layers >=15 are causally inert for the final position.
prediction: Perturbing resid_pre at non-final positions for any layer >=15 changes final logits by exactly 0; at layers <=14 by >0.
falsification: Any nonzero change at layers >=15 under perturbation.
alternatives: Implementation detail of transformers version (e.g. cache path) differs from reference implementation
evidence: experiments/E001_arch/result.json

statement: Factual recall shows ROME-style early site (last subject token, middle layers) and late site (final token) under counterfactual patching.
prediction: See E004 PREREG P1-P2.
falsification: Recovery <0.5 at all last-subject-token layers in >30% of pairs.
alternatives: Distributed recall without localized site
Answer copied from PLE token identity
evidence: experiments/E004_factual_patching/analysis.json
note: E004: late site supported (P2 12/12), early site P1 failed narrowly (8/12 < 70%); the third-prompt control is not a zero null (AUDIT-001) and gave 0.15-0.36 'recovery'; E004b needed.

statement: Subject enrichment usable by later positions must be complete by layer 14 because later layers cannot read new K/V.
prediction: E004 P3; restoring only layer-13/14 K/V at subject positions recovers most of the effect.
falsification: Patching subject positions at layers 13/14 has small effect while earlier layers have large effect AND final-position late-layer patching does not explain the gap.
alternatives: Information moved to final position before layer 14 so subject K/V is irrelevant later
evidence: E006: what matters is the layer-13 K/V at subject positions (layer 13 is the last layer whose sliding K/V is read), consistent with 'enrichment must complete by layer 13' but enrichment itself was not measured
note: E004 P3 passed (median recovery at layer 14 = 0.005 vs max 0.93) but this is expected from frozen K/V alone; superseded by H-008.

statement: E2B contains induction heads causally necessary for in-context copying of random token sequences.
prediction: E003 PREREG P1-P4.
falsification: Top-5 induction-head ablation not larger than random-5 ablations.
alternatives: Copying distributed across many heads (redundancy)
PLE/positional shortcuts

statement: Logit-lens answer emergence occurs in the last third of layers in Gemma 4 E2B.
prediction: E002 PREREG P1-P3.
falsification: Median first top-1 layer < 24.
alternatives: Logit lens bias in models with layer_scalar / sandwich norms
evidence: experiments/E002_logit_lens/analysis.json

statement: Per-layer embeddings re-inject token identity at every layer, so residual-stream-only interventions underestimate token-identity effects.
prediction: Patching residual + PLE at a position recovers more than residual alone at late layers <=14.
falsification: No difference between residual-only and residual+PLE patching.
alternatives: PLE contribution small relative to residual

statement: The k/v tensors stored for KV-shared layers in the checkpoint are untrained remnants.
prediction: Their statistics match an initialization distribution and are identical or near-identical between IT and base checkpoints.
falsification: Statistics resemble trained layers or differ systematically between IT and base.
alternatives: Trained weights from a pre-sharing training phase then frozen
evidence: experiments/E001_arch/result.json

statement: Subject information used for factual recall reaches the final position through the sliding-window K/V produced by layer 13, not through the full-attention K/V produced by layer 14.
prediction: Patching only layer-13 K/V at subject positions (clean→corrupt) restores most of the effect seen when patching resid_pre of layer 13; patching only layer-14 K/V restores ~0.
falsification: Layer-14 K/V patch restores as much as or more than layer-13 K/V patch, or neither restores much (effect lives in another path).
alternatives: Resid-pre-13 patch acts through layer-13 MLP→layer-14 K/V interaction rather than layer-13 K/V
Recovery reflects corrupt-answer suppression rather than clean restoration (E004 control issue)
evidence: experiments/E004_factual_patching/analysis.json: mean recovery at last subject token 0.595 (layer 13) vs 0.010 (layer 14)

E006 (preregistered, 28 held-out pairs incl. 16 R2 pairs never used before): KV13_all median recovery 0.986 [subject-cluster CI 0.947-0.995] vs KV14_all 0.017; KV13_D 0.980, KV13_T 0.006; NULL max|r| 1.1e-6 -> K-0006

statement: Transfer of subject information into the final position completes in block 25 (a sliding-attention layer reading layer-13 K/V): restoring the final-position residual is ineffective before block 25 and near-complete after it.
prediction: Ablating/patching block-25 attention output at the final position removes most of the recall effect; logit-lens answer emergence (median index 28) follows the transfer.
falsification: Block-25 attention ablation at the final position has small effect on recall LD.
alternatives: Transfer distributed over blocks 15-25 with the final position only 'decodable' after 25
Metric artefact of LD-based recovery (control reaches 0.37-0.46 at the same layers)
evidence: experiments/E004_factual_patching/analysis.json: final-position mean recovery 0.056 at resid_pre 25 vs 0.846 at resid_pre 26

E006: patching block-25 attention at the final position recovers 0.757 [0.654-0.826], the largest ATTN_L in 28/28 pairs (all other L <= 0.05 median); noising it in the clean run retains only 0.227 [0.155-0.306] -> K-0007
E006b: specificity confirmed (other layers' noising retains >=0.929) but mean ablation retains 0.84 -> sufficient/dominant, not necessary; K-0007 revised

statement: Head 0 of block 25 is the dominant subject-attribute extraction head in Gemma 4 E2B factual recall.
prediction: Patching HEAD25_0 alone recovers >=0.4 (observed exploratory 0.48); its attention at the final position concentrates on subject positions; ablating it alone reduces LD more than any other single block-25 head.
falsification: Attention of head 25.0 not concentrated on the subject span, or single-head noising of 25.0 retains >0.8.
alternatives: Non-additivity of the post-attention RMSNorm makes single-head patching misleading (the RMS of the summed output changes)
Several heads share the role redundantly and 25.0 only dominates on these templates
evidence: E006 exploratory HEAD25 sweep: head 0 median 0.483 [cluster CI 0.326-0.601]; heads 1-7 <= 0.007

E006b: head-0 subject attention mass median 0.88 vs uniform 0.17 (prereg Q1 pass); single-head noising retained 0.37 vs >=0.98 for heads 1-7 (Q4, exploratory). Not in KB: no mean-ablation at head level, no audit.
E006c: heads 1-7 jointly corrupted retain 0.96; head-0 mean-ablation retains 0.89; head-0 mass on verified subject span 0.87 (100% of pairs >= 3x uniform) -> folded into K-0007

statement: Because block 25 reads the layer-13 *sliding* (512-token window) K/V, a subject placed more than 512 tokens before the query cannot be retrieved through the block-25 route; recall then must use the layer-14 full-attention K/V (blocks 19/24/29/34) or fail.
prediction: Contextual recall with subject at distance >512: KV14 patch recovery rises from ~0.02 to >=0.5 and ATTN_25 patch recovery falls below 0.2; accuracy drops relative to distance <512.
falsification: At distance >512 the KV14 route stays ~0 while recall remains correct (another route exists).
alternatives: The model copies subject identity into template tokens within the window before layer 13 (then KV13 at template positions would carry it)
Recall fails entirely beyond the window without rerouting
evidence: Architectural: sliding_window=512 for layer 13 (config); E006 shows recall at short range uses only KV13

statement: For multi-token subjects, the answer-relevant information in the layer-13 K/V is distributed over the subject span rather than concentrated at the last subject token.
prediction: KV13_S (last subject token only) recovers much less than KV13_D for multi-token subjects but not for single-token subjects.
falsification: KV13_S ~ KV13_D for multi-token subjects on new data.
alternatives: Last-token enrichment is incomplete at layer 13 but completes later (invisible to shared layers)
Template-specific effect of landmark names
evidence: E006 (exploratory): KV13_S median 0.386 for R1 multi-token landmarks vs 0.980 for R2 (mostly single-token countries); KV13_D 0.981/0.980; relates to H-002 P1 failure (E004)
H014 spectroscopy: KV13_S is the dominant axis of pair-to-pair variation in both checkpoints (loading -0.94 on component 1, 59% of centred variance)

statement: In-context (prompt-defined) associations and parametric facts use the same layer-13 K/V -> block-25 route.
prediction: For 'X is paired with Y ... X is paired with' style prompts, KV13_D recovery >= 0.7 and KV14 <= 0.2 (MiniMax HYPGEN-01); competing prediction (DeepSeek HYPGEN-01): in-context binding relies on layer-14 full K/V (KV14 >= 0.5).
falsification: Neither KV13 nor KV14 alone recovers >= 0.5 for in-context items, or the two generators' predictions are both wrong.
alternatives: Induction-style copying through full-attention layers 19/24/29/34 (E003 found induction heads at 24.1 and 29.5)
Mixed routes depending on distance
evidence: agents/reports/HYPGEN-01.md: competing predictions from two model families; to be tested in E008 together with H-011

statement: Causal-effect spectroscopy: the matrix of single-site intervention effects (pairs x sites) has low-rank modular structure whose components align with functional modules (e.g. subject K/V route, block-25 extraction, late readout). [cycle-3 test: strong form not confirmed]
prediction: On E004/E006 effect matrices, >= 80% of variance in <= 3 components, with loadings separating layer-13 K/V / block-25 / late-layer sites.
falsification: Effect matrix is near full-rank or components do not map onto separable site groups.
alternatives: Low rank is an artefact of the recovery normalisation (shared denominator)
Structure reflects prompt templates rather than mechanisms
evidence: DeepSeek HYPGEN-01 'radical principle' proposal; testable on existing data at ~0 CPU cost

meta_analysis/H014_spectroscopy (prereg): centred E006 matrix (80 pairs x 36 sites, IT+base) top-3 = 0.832 vs column-permutation null p99 0.804 (median 0.79) -> all 4 prereg criteria nominally pass, but the margin is small and component 1 is ~one column (KV13_S, the multi-token subject effect of H-012). Exploratory standardised analysis: top-3 = 0.40 vs null 0.21 -> real co-variation beyond marginals but not low-rank/modular in the strong sense. IT->base transfer of components 0.80 vs random-subspace p99 0.22 (weak null). Prereg typo: 44 columns stated, 36 exist.

statement: A backup route carries subject information to the answer when block-25 subject content is removed (mean ablation retains 0.84).
prediction: Under MEAN_ATTN25, a second site (candidate: full-attention layers reading layer-14 K/V, or block-25 heads 2/6 with subject mass 0.55/0.51) becomes necessary: additional mean-ablation there drops retained below 0.4.
falsification: No combination of additional single-layer mean ablations reduces retained below 0.6.
alternatives: Relation-level priors in the mean vector plus residual subject signal before layer 15
Distributed weak contributions across many layers
evidence: E006c C4: no single additional KV-shared attention layer brings retained below 0.74 (min JOINT_25_31 0.743); mean-ablating all 20 KV-shared attention layers retains 0.46 -> the 'second site' prediction is refuted; the non-late-attention share must come from layers 0-14 (final-position attention to subject tokens) and/or late MLPs (H-016)

statement: About half of the subject->answer effect in E2B factual recall is carried into the final-position residual by layers 0-14 (final-position attention to subject tokens before KV sharing), and is read out by late MLPs, independently of KV-shared attention.
prediction: Mean-ablating final-position attention in layers 0-14 together with all KV-shared attention drops retained from 0.46 to <= 0.15; ablating only layers 0-14 final-position attention retains >= 0.7 (block 25 compensates).
falsification: Joint ablation of early+late final-position attention still retains >= 0.35.
alternatives: Prompt-generic relation priors in the mean vectors carry the answer (test: resample-ablation instead of mean)
Late MLPs recompute the answer from PLE/token identity of the final token (not subject-specific)
evidence: E006c LATE_ALL_MEAN 0.46 [0.40, 0.51]; E004 final-position resid patches at L<=14 recover ~0 only in the presence of conflicting subject K/V

statement: In Gemma 4 E2B-IT, the final decoder block(s) (34, partly 33) shift next-token probability from the factual content token toward chat-style formatting/answer-form tokens (' **', first names, initials, articles) on raw-completion prompts; this shift is a product of instruction tuning and is absent or much weaker in the base checkpoint.
prediction: Base checkpoint on factset_v1: (i) fraction of errors whose final top-1 is ' **' or another markdown token < 2% (IT: see E009 exploratory); (ii) accuracy at residual 33 minus final accuracy <= 2 points (IT: +6 points TEST); (iii) the number of 'lost answers' (target top-1 at some layer 20-34 but not final) at most half of IT's 151.
falsification: Base shows the same late-layer answer loss (>= +4 points at residual 33) and similar formatting top-1s.
alternatives: Late-layer answer loss is a generic property of the logit lens at layer 33 vs 35 (lens miscalibration), not of IT
Base also prefers first names/articles; only the markdown share is IT-specific
evidence: E009 exploratory_errors.json (post hoc): DEV acc by residual index peaks at 33 (0.476) vs final 0.375; TEST 0.475 vs 0.414; 151/480 errors had the target top-1 at some residual 20-34; lost-answer peaks at residual 33-34; error top-1s include ' **', ' Herman', ' J'

statement: Internal stability signals (layer from which the top-1 stops changing, logit-lens agreement over residuals 26-35, block-25 head-0 attention entropy) detect Gemma 4 E2B-IT first-token errors better than softmax confidence.
prediction: On a new item set with knowledge-only correctness (answer-form errors excluded), combined detector AUROC - maxprob AUROC >= 0.03 with a relation-clustered CI excluding 0.
falsification: Clustered CI includes 0 on a larger relation set, or the gain disappears once answer-form errors are removed.
alternatives: Signals detect answer-form (formatting) responses rather than knowledge errors
Gain driven by a few relations (relation-level confound)
evidence: E009 TEST: combined 0.807 vs maxprob 0.709; item-iid CI of difference [0.050, 0.147] (prereg P-a1 pass); relation-clustered CI [-0.029, 0.232] includes 0 (AUDIT-004 follow-up); best single signal S3 0.775

E009 exploratory_knowledge_vs_form_it.json (post hoc): 77/232 TEST errors are answer-form errors; on the remaining 319 items (155 knowledge errors) maxprob AUROC 0.707, lens agreement S2 0.708 (advantage gone), first-stable-layer S3 0.734, DEV-fit combined 0.787 -> part of the internal-signal advantage was detection of answer form. Retest must use knowledge-only scoring and relation-clustered CIs.

statement: The IT-specific late answer-form shift (H-017) is implemented by final-position MLP/PLE outputs of blocks 26-34, not by the layer-13 -> block-25 retrieval route: patching base-checkpoint late-block MLP outputs into the IT run restores the factual first token.
prediction: On factset items where IT final top-1 is an answer-form token but the target is top-1 at residual 33: patching base mlp_out (blocks 33-34, final position) into IT makes the target top-1 in >= 50% of items; patching base layer-13 K/V does not (< 10%).
falsification: Late MLP cross-patching restores < 20% while attention/K-V cross-patching restores more.
alternatives: IT changed the final norm/unembedding geometry rather than block outputs (test: lens with base final norm)
Shift distributed across all late layers so no block subset suffices
evidence: HYPGEN-02 (DeepSeek + MiniMax converge); E009 exploratory: target peaks at residual 33-34 in lost answers

statement: Cross-architecture transfer: in models with a shared cross-position memory interface (KV-sharing sources, MLA latent cache, SSM state), subject evidence used for factual recall is written at the last layer able to alter that shared state and extracted by a later reader layer at the answer position.
prediction: In small public models of each class (<= 1B params, CPU), restoring the shared state written by the last writer layer at subject positions recovers >= 0.8 of the logit difference, while earlier writers alone recover <= 0.3.
falsification: Recovery peaks at a non-final writer or is spread across writers in >= 2 of 3 architecture classes.
alternatives: Gemma's single-layer localisation is specific to its 13/14 sharing layout
SSMs integrate subject information continuously (no single writer)
evidence: K-0006 (Gemma 4 E2B: layer-13 K/V is the sole carrier); ROME-in-Mamba two-site pattern (LIT06-022); HYPGEN-02 convergence
